Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(Entertainment Weekly) -- J.J. Abrams' franchise reboot boldly went where no Star Trek movie has gone before, grossing a stellar $72.5 million from Friday through Sunday, according to early estimates by Hollywood.com Box Office. In the film, Spock (Zachary Quinto, left) and Kirk get off on the wrong foot. That's the second-best opening of 2009 (after X-Men Origins: Wolverine's $85.1 million last weekend), and it includes a whopping $8.2 million earned in IMAX showings, a new one-weekend record for the large format (beating The Dark Knight's $6.3 million). What's more, if you add in the $4 million that the movie starring Chris Pine and Zachary Quinto earned in late-Thursday showings, Star Trek has banked an impressive $76.5 million so far -- well ahead of most expectations. This result is highly logical. Considering all the hype and buzz and strong reviews that Star Trek has garnered, it's no surprise that this film's opening sum is by far the biggest of any Star Trek movie: Of the 10 previous flicks in the franchise, 1996's Star Trek: First Contact bowed best, with (only) $30.7 million over three days. Moreover, a look at the movie's CinemaScore report card reveals some potentially good news. While it drew an expected crowd mostly comprised of older males, Star Trek's solid-A grade shows that word of mouth could be strong enough to bring in fans outside of the franchise's usual demographic (i.e. people who weren't alive in the 1980s...and women) as the weeks go on. Unless said folks are too distracted by Angels & Demons, Night at the Museum 2, and all the other big flicks on tap, of course. X-Men Origins: Wolverine (No. 2) was next with $27 million on a 68 percent decline. Fanboy-driven films always fall hard, but this drop is particularly hefty. Nevertheless, Hugh Jackman's franchise flick has already banked $129.6 million in 10 days. Fellow holdovers Ghosts of Girlfriends Past (No. 3 with $10.5 million), Obsessed (No. 4 with $6.6 million), and 17 Again (No. 5 with $4.4 million) rounded out the top five. And the comedy Next Day Air failed to take off, grossing just $4 million at No. 6. And in limited release, neither Rudo y Cursi nor Little Ashes made much of a mark, as each averaged well under $7,000 per theater. Overall, the box office was up nearly 22 percent from the same frame a year ago (when the infamous Speed Racer hit a bump in the road). And, really, what could be a better Mother's Day gift than that? Love ya, Mom! Have a great day! CLICK HERE to Try 2 RISK FREE issues of Entertainment Weekly . ## ‘Star Trek’ beams up a franchise-best $72.5 million at weekend box office

**LOS ANGELES —** Paramount’s *Star Trek* boldly went where no film in the long-running sci-fi franchise had gone before, opening to an estimated **$72.5 million** at the domestic box office over the weekend.

The J.J. Abrams-directed reboot easily claimed the No. 1 spot and delivered the biggest opening in *Star Trek* history, far surpassing previous franchise launches such as *Star Trek: First Contact*, which debuted with about **$30.7 million** in 1996, and *Star Trek: Nemesis*, which opened to roughly **$18.5 million** in 2002.

The film also scored strongly with premium-format audiences. Its IMAX run brought in a record-setting haul for the format at the time, with *Star Trek* posting an impressive IMAX opening from a relatively limited number of giant-screen locations. That performance underscored the movie’s appeal not only to longtime Trekkers, but also to general audiences looking for a big-screen summer spectacle.

Audience reaction appeared strong as well: *Star Trek* earned an **“A” CinemaScore**, suggesting solid word of mouth in the weeks ahead. That’s especially important for a franchise relaunch that sought to introduce younger viewers to characters like James T. Kirk, Spock, Uhura, and Dr. McCoy while still satisfying longtime fans.

The opening marked a major turnaround for a series that had struggled theatrically in recent years. While earlier *Star Trek* films generally performed respectably, none had opened anywhere near this level. The new film’s $72.5 million debut put it in blockbuster territory and signaled that Paramount’s gamble on a faster, younger, more action-driven reboot had paid off.

With its strong reviews, enthusiastic audience grades, and record-setting IMAX numbers, *Star Trek* entered the summer movie season as one of the year’s early breakout hits — and gave the venerable franchise a powerful new beginning.

The opening easily surpassed expectations and marked a major win for Paramount as the summer movie season entered its second frame.

# ‘Star Trek’ Blasts Past Expectations With $76.5 Million Opening

J.J. Abrams’ reboot of *Star Trek* launched the long-running sci-fi franchise into a new box-office orbit over the weekend, exceeding industry expectations with an estimated $76.5 million total, including Thursday night previews.

The Paramount release, starring Chris Pine as James T. Kirk and Zachary Quinto as Spock, had been expected to open strongly, but its debut outpaced many forecasts and signaled that Abrams’ attempt to broaden the franchise beyond its core fan base had paid off. Strong reviews, upbeat word of mouth and a high-profile marketing campaign helped turn *Star Trek* into the weekend’s clear No. 1 film.

The opening marks a major revival for a property that had struggled theatrically in recent years. By emphasizing younger characters, large-scale action and a more accessible origin-story approach, the new *Star Trek* drew both longtime fans and newcomers.

In second place, *X-Men Origins: Wolverine* fell sharply in its second weekend, taking in about $27 million. The Hugh Jackman-led superhero film remained a major player at the box office, though its steep drop suggested mixed word of mouth after a huge debut.

Romantic comedy *Ghosts of Girlfriends Past*, starring Matthew McConaughey and Jennifer Garner, landed in third with roughly $10.5 million. The film continued to appeal to date-night audiences, though it faced tough competition from the weekend’s blockbuster launch.

The thriller *Obsessed*, featuring Beyoncé Knowles, Idris Elba and Ali Larter, took fourth place with about $6.6 million, adding to its solid domestic run after opening at No. 1 earlier in the season.

Rounding out the top five was *17 Again*, the Zac Efron comedy, which earned approximately $4.4 million. The film continued to show staying power among younger moviegoers and family audiences.

But the weekend belonged decisively to *Star Trek*. With a $76.5 million start and strong audience response, Paramount appears to have successfully reintroduced one of Hollywood’s most recognizable science-fiction brands for a new generation.
